chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Bribery in judgment is disbelief in God.

key_terms.الرِّشَا: Bribery — giving money or gifts to influence a judge's ruling; broadly encompasses both giving and receiving bribes in a judicial context
key_terms.الْحُكْمِ: Judgment/ruling — specifically judicial pronouncements made by a judge (qadi); the word encompasses both the process and the verdict
key_terms.الْكُفْرُ بِاللَّهِ: Disbelief in God — the highest category of moral and theological transgression in Islamic law; using this term signals the utmost severity of the sin

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about bribery in judgment or judicial proceedings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers a stark pronouncement equating bribery in judicial proceedings with disbelief (kufr) in God. This emphatic statement reflects the Imam's concern for the integrity of the Islamic justice system. In the context of early Islamic jurisprudence, where judges (qadis) held immense authority and public trust, any corruption of that office through bribery was seen as a betrayal not merely of law, but of the divine order itself.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zurara, from sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The briber regarding the judgement, he is the disbeliever in Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from his brother al-Hassan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah, who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Accepting a bribe to issue a judgment is denial of the existence of Allah.’”
